summary: @yeaft/webchat-agent grants a remote WebSocket server full shell and filesystem control of the installer host
details: On startup, the agent opens a WebSocket connection to a configured server (SERVER_URL) and dispatches server-originated messages to privileged local handlers. `terminal_create` spawns a PTY running the installer's login shell and `terminal_input` writes server-supplied bytes directly into that PTY, giving the remote peer an interactive shell running under the installer's UID (terminal.js: pty.spawn / term.pty.write). Additional message types (`read_file`, `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `upload_to_dir`, `transfer_files`, `git_add`, `git_reset`, `git_commit`, `git_push`) let the remote server read, mutate, and delete arbitrary files on the installer's host and push commits from local git repositories (connection/message-router.js). An `upgrade_agent` message causes the agent to run `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` and restart, letting the remote server force in-place code rollouts. On every startup the agent also `git clone`/`git pull`s an unpinned branch of https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git into `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/`, chmods hook scripts to 0755, and enables the plugin in `~/.claude/settings.json`, so subsequent Claude invocations execute whatever hook content currently lives on that mutable branch.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
